newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts aim for 111-10 but must hold 110-10.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts aim for 111-10 but must hold 110-10.

text.p: British gilts have the potential to rally further on Thursday, provided they can hold above the key 110-10 level, technical analysts said.
The market will soon bump into resistance around 110-28, but if it jumps that, should climb towards 111-10, 12, they added.
"The performance in gilts yesterday was very impressive and there was a significant break-out of the recent high at 110-10," said Adrian Sells, director of Crane Investment Analysis.
"It's important we maintain that advance and build on it." The market has had trouble hurdling the April 17 high at 110-10, but swept through it on Wednesday to a high of 110-26.
By 0715 GMT, the June gilt future was up 1/32 at 110-20.
"I can see resistance initially starting around the 110-28 area, the lows back in March before the market broke down to the 110-04 level," said Sells.
Charts show the contract hit a daily low of 110-28 on March 7 and March 14 before sliding to a low of 110-04 on March 17.
Sells said a push through 110-28 would open up the potential for a move to 111-10,12.
"The only damage the market could do would be to start trading down below 110-10 again and close below there," said Sells. "That break-out needs to be maintained today."
He put support around 110-06,04 then 109-26, the low on Wednesday. "But barring a tremendous upset in the election today, the market looks set to rally further," he said.
British voters go to the polls on Thursday.
Juliette Clarke at the Royal Bank of Scotland agreed Wednesday's gains meant technicals now strongly favoured the bull side.
"The Gann charts now point to a time and price objective set at 111-17 for next Wednesday/Thursday," she said in a daily comment for clients.
Gann analysis is a method which uses trendlines from price tops or bottoms at specific angles to predict levels.
"Even if the market falls sharply tomorrow after the election the recent gains have formed a buffer and the bull view will hold, even on a dip as far as 109-04/05," said Clarke
Clarke put resistance at 110-29 and then 111-00,01. "It is likely that these levels will form a strong barrier today as new buyers will be thin on the ground," she said.
By 0732 GMT, June short sterling was down 0.01 at 93.38. Analysts said the bull phase may continue, but added holidays across Europe and election jitters may cap gains near term.
